description: Phase 2-3 walk-through on northwind-retail / llm-inference-efficiency. Thread one: the lead writes three slide briefs and composes them (designer, default design); the owner says it looks generic; the lead proposes two design directions (system layer palettes, designer samples on slide 2); the owner picks B; the slides are stale and are recomposed in it. Thread two: a recap from state, then 'Retitle slide 2 to ...' goes by rule to the mechanic, without the lead. Owner messages, in order: anything (turn 1), anything (turn 2), pick B of p0001 with the button, anything (turn 4); new thread; 'Retitle slide 2 to Quantisation cuts the bill by 38%'.

steps.label: t1 u1: create the deck and write three briefs

brief.header: Northwind can serve its shopping assistant at 38% lower cost
brief.intent: The opening: before anyone speaks, the reader knows who the proposal is for and what it promises: the same assistant at 38% lower cost, $4.20 per 1,000 answers falling to $2.60.

points: A proposal to Northwind Retail · November 2026

brief.notes: A title slide. $2.60 is the new state and matters more than $4.20.

brief.header: Quantisation alone cuts serving cost by 38%
brief.intent: The single biggest saving comes from one technique: 8-bit weights take monthly serving cost from $412k to $255k without changing the answers.

points: Same answer quality on 2,000 test questions

brief.notes: 38% is the hero; the before and after is quieter evidence.

brief.header: What it costs and what it returns
brief.intent: The business case is simple: a one-off cost of $310k is repaid in about two months by a saving of $1.9M a year.

points: Engineering $240k and evaluation $70k; the saving is $157k a month from the first full month

brief.notes: Read left to right as cost, return, payback; the return matters most.

arguments.summary: Two directions for the look of the deck

directions.name: Itemised
directions.concept: Every slide reads like a till receipt for its claim: the evidence itemised line by line, and the one total that matters marked in carbon blue.
rules: The background is receipt paper; a carbon-blue field may carry the header.
Carbon blue marks exactly one figure per slide.
No icons, no rounded cards: fields, rules and type do the work.

directions.name: Demand curve
directions.concept: The assistant's traffic over a day is what the bill follows, so each slide is built along one line on a night-blue ground, with peach marking the one thing to look at.
rules: The background is night blue; each slide has one dominant horizontal line.
Peach marks exactly one thing per slide; everything else is cool grey or blue.
No boxes around text; at least a third of the slide stays empty.

roles.dk1: print: figures and secondary text. Safe on lt1 and lt2.
roles.lt1: receipt paper: the slide background; also text on accent1.
roles.dk2: faded print: body text and labels; charts label in it. Safe on lt1.
roles.lt2: counter: a quiet panel. Text on it in dk1.
roles.accent1: carbon blue: the header field and the one figure that matters. Safe as text on lt1.
roles.accent2: highlighter: a stripe behind one total. Never text.
roles.accent4: slate: a second chart series. Not for text.
roles.accent5: pale paper: a quiet panel. Not for text.
roles.accent6: printed grey: chart neutral and thin rules. Not for text.

roles.dk1: ink: not readable on the night ground; unused for text here.
roles.lt1: paper: headers and large figures. Safe on lt2 and accent4.
roles.dk2: mist, a light colour: body text and labels; charts label in it. Safe on lt2.
roles.lt2: night: the slide background. A ground, not a text colour.
roles.accent1: curve peach: the line and the one figure that matters. Safe on lt2.
roles.accent2: before blue: the old state in a comparison. Safe on lt2.
roles.accent3: faint rule: the dominant line and ticks. Never text.
roles.accent4: dusk: a faint band. Text on it in lt1.
roles.accent5: deep dusk: a stronger band. Not for text.
roles.accent6: slate: chart neutral. Not for text.
